correctness.rationale: For q>3, the source gives dual distance 3, so generator columns are distinct projective points in PG(3,q). Minimality is equivalent to the hyperplane zero section spanning its plane. The source weight spectrum gives section sizes 2q-2,q,q-1,q-2,0. The q(q-1) class is exactly c(0,b); its q-1 zero columns are shown directly from the trace model to lie on one projective line. Sections of size 2q-2 exceed a line. A hyperplane-pencil count rules out a line-contained q-section, and a deficit refinement combined with the proven q-1 line sections rules out a line-contained q-2 section. Full-weight words are nonminimal. The q=3 family is reduced by cyclic multipliers to the canonical code. Standard-library replay over q=3,5,7,11 agrees in every exponent-ratio class tested.

value.rationale: The primary article explicitly identifies this exact question as future work after proving the canonical case. The result resolves that question for the entire infinite family over every odd prime power, gives an intrinsic projective explanation independent of the special perfect-nonlinear equivalence, and yields an exact closed count of minimal codewords. Because covering structures control the minimal access sets in the paper's secret-sharing application, the extension is structurally and cryptographically relevant rather than a routine parameter check.
